items.item_text: Guided Pathways and related practices.
Provides a full range of specialized support to District’s financial aid programs and functions. Function as a technical expert in assigned areas of financial aid processing.
Role of higher education, and specifically community colleges, in supporting marginalized populations.
Learn and understand in-depth student financial aid processes and procedures including laws, regulations, and District policies and procedures.
Equity frameworks and practices in higher education.
Apply an equity-minded framework and ensure programs, services and processes are designed and delivered to meet the varying needs of all eligible students.
Current higher education equity-based retention and success trends, including issues, strategies, regulations, and compliance in the state, regionally, nationally, and internationally.
Coordinate operations and activities of the Basic Needs Program; implement procedures for the day-to-day operations of assigned program areas on as as needed basis.
General accounting and bookkeeping practices and techniques used in ledger recordkeeping. State and federal tax returns, schedules, and attachments.
Perform arithmetic calculations of average to above average difficulty.
Needs analysis methodology.
Make oral presentations to groups.
Methods to successfully support students with disabilities.
Adapt to changing technologies and learn functionality of new equipment and systems.
Office procedures, methods, and equipment including computers and applicable software applications such as word processing, spreadsheets, and databases.
Type or enter data at a speed necessary for successful job performance.
Financial aid management systems and a variety of specialized off-campus software applications.
Maintain close attention to detail.
Mathematical principles and practices.
Properly handle difficult, sensitive, and confidential situations and materials.
English usage, spelling, grammar and punctuation.
Plan, organize and prioritize work in order to meet schedules and timelines.
Principles and procedures of record keeping and filing.
Maintain current, accurate and confidential records and files including financial records.
Principles of business letter writing and basic report preparation.
Conduct technical research and prepare a variety of comprehensive and statistical reports.
Pertinent federal, state, and local laws, codes, and regulations including state and federal labor law as it applies to the employment of students and DHS employment requirements and documentation.
Independently prepare routine correspondence and memoranda.
Management and leadership concepts and practices, including change management, organizational and motivational techniques;
Work independently and collaboratively.
Personnel management practices and techniques of supervision and staff evaluation;
Supervise student and/or other temporary help.
Employment processes, collective bargaining processes, data collection, and report writing; and Safety practices.
Establish and maintain effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of work.
In-depth knowledge of state and federal student financial aid processes and procedures including federal and state laws and regulations regarding the various duties of the Financial Aid Office.
Operate office equipment including computers and supporting word processing, spreadsheet, and database applications.
Human relations skills, methods, and techniques to conduct interviews, convey technical information, resolve conflicts, and to facilitate problem resolution.
Communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing.
